text[1]: The required vertex sequence for spline-fit and curve-fit POLYLINEs is illustrated — vertex ordering matters and differs between the two types.
Layer polyline-light indicates a polyline that is converted to LWPOLYLINE if PLINETYPE sysvar is the default (2) when the drawing is reopened.

POLYLINE #1 is a 20×7 polygon mesh (int[71]=20, int[72]=7). Exactly M×N = 140 VERTEX rows (int[70]=64) must follow. int[71] and int[72] must match the actual vertex count — a mismatch produces a corrupt mesh in both DXF and DWG output.

On LWPOLYLINE, int[70]=128 means closed (same bit position as POLYLINE linetype-pattern flag but different meaning). On POLYLINE int[70]=128 enables continuous linetype pattern generation (2D only). On LWPOLYLINE int[70]=1 means closed and int[70]=128 is not used — prefer int[70]=1 for closed LWPOLYLINE.

An AI generating a simple 2D open or closed polyline should prefer LWPOLYLINE over POLYLINE. LWPOLYLINE is the modern equivalent: no VERTEX or SEQEND rows required, all vertices in a single pt[10] field, int[70]=1 for closed. Use POLYLINE only when you need 3D vertices, mesh, spline-fit, or curve-fit.
